Context: this is NOT a build-step test — it's Phase 2 of a PR REVIEW (zimmerMANNReview skill) for someone else's already-open pull request. Read-only. Do not write or edit any code. Report findings only.

## What you're reviewing
GitHub PR #65 in ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa: "feat(header): global header rebuild — shell, logo, Contentful nav data, close-state contract (SFCC-52/746/747)". Author: Tim Lavelle (TimLavelleACC). 104 files changed, +10187/-745. Base branch: develop.

Two git worktrees are already set up so you don't need to fetch/checkout anything:
- HEAD (the PR's tip, commit 10eb79dc881b3e3881d528ee661090779dc11b9d): /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-marcel-a-n-navarro-Dev-zimmermann-pwa/bfb1292b-bdc6-483e-a9c4-1846dc9424fe/scratchpad/pr65-head
- BASE (develop, commit 269d5d40149b9947111dd87e78d37b92fccd4c99): /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-marcel-a-n-navarro-Dev-zimmermann-pwa/bfb1292b-bdc6-483e-a9c4-1846dc9424fe/scratchpad/pr65-base

Use `git diff 269d5d40149b9947111dd87e78d37b92fccd4c99 10eb79dc881b3e3881d528ee661090779dc11b9d -- <path>` from the main repo (/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa) to see diffs, or read files directly in the two worktrees for full context.

## Gates already measured — DO NOT RE-RUN THEM, use these numbers
- `npx tsc --noEmit`: clean on both base and head.
- `npm run lint`: base = 20 problems (4 errors, 16 warnings, all pre-existing debt unrelated to this PR — routes.tsx, recipeGuards.test.ts, old header/index.tsx, product-view/index.tsx, product-detail/index.tsx). Head = 24 problems (5 errors, 19 warnings). The NEW issues introduced by this PR (i.e. not present at base) are: `useHeaderNav.test.ts:106` prettier error (new), `drawer-menu/index.stories.tsx` 2 non-null-assertion warnings (new), `drawer-menu/index.tsx:135` unused-var warning for `_onLogoClick` (new — see finding below), `header/rightBar/index.tsx` 2 unused-var warnings for `storeLocatorEnabled`/`onStoreLocatorClick` (new — see finding below), `useHeaderNav.ts:64` non-null-assertion warning (new, but has a justifying inline comment — I consider this one acceptable, not a defect, per typescript.md's rule; feel free to double check the comment still holds up).
- `node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs`: base = 4 unacknowledged raw-value violations (all in files this PR deletes/renames away — header/index.tsx, the old theme/components/header.ts, navConstants.ts). Head = 1 unacknowledged violation: `overrides/app/components/footer/footer.css.ts:20` — `const BP_CONTENT_WRAP = '59.125em'; // 946px`, introduced fresh by this PR's tip commit (see scope finding below), with no audit-allow/provisional/pending comment on that specific line even though the surrounding code says "No confirmed Figma frame yet." Verify whether this should count as an acknowledged exception per the script's own rules (comment block containing "provisional"/"pending"/"placeholder"/"audit-allow") — my read is it does NOT qualify, confirm or correct me.
- `npm run test` (Vitest): base = 26 files / 408 tests, all passing. Head = 41 files / 612 tests, all passing. No regressions, substantial new coverage.
- CI (`gh pr checks 65`): Unit tests, Storybook interaction & a11y tests, tsc/lint-adjacent checks all pass. Both Playwright E2E jobs (localhost and BrowserStack) show "skipping" — this PR gets zero automated E2E coverage before merge (a documented trade-off of this repo's change-scoped E2E design when a diff spans multiple areas, not a bug in the CI itself, but worth weighing given the size of this PR).

## Requirements context (already gathered from Jira, condensed)
- **SFCC-52** ("Global Header UI"): header shell/layout only — structure, placement, sticky behaviour. Icon *destinations* wired up in later stories. Logo links home. No explicit Figma node link in the ticket itself (just an attached reference screenshot, "Figma is leading") — this is a real gap, escalated separately, not yours to solve.
- **SFCC-746** ("Navigation – PWA Kit & Contentful"): supersedes the nav portion of SFCC-52. Top-level nav items managed in Contentful, keyed by SFCC category ID. Figma UI Kit node: 2083-53877 (Zimmermann_Design_System_2026 file). Explicitly OUT of scope: "hover/focus/active visual states (defined in UI kit)" — i.e. don't expect this PR to hand-roll those, they should come from the UI kit's own component recipe. Mega-menu behaviour and mobile hamburger/drill-down are explicitly called out in SFCC-746's own text as SFCC-96's scope, not 746's.
- **SFCC-747** ("Logo Masthead"): supersedes the logo portion of SFCC-52. Static brand asset, not Contentful-managed. Figma node: 2083-53927. Scroll behaviour explicitly out of scope (→ SFCC-93). Hover/focus states defined in UI kit, not repeated here.
- **SFCC-93** (scroll behaviour): status "To Do", no design AC yet — PR correctly excludes this.
- **SFCC-96** ("Expanded Navigation - PWA Kit and Contentful", status "Ready For Review"): desktop mega-menu (two-column panel: subcategory + editorial links left, campaign image right, all Contentful-managed) AND — per **SFCC-97 being archived into it** ("Archiving as all breakpoints are covered in SFCC-96") — mobile hamburger drill-down too. **This PR's `list-menu/megaMenuContent/` and `drawer-menu/` appear to substantially implement SFCC-96's full described scope** (Contentful-driven mega-menu with subcategory/editorial links + campaign image, full mobile drill-down with back navigation), but the PR title/body only claims SFCC-52/746/747 and never mentions SFCC-96. This is a scope-tracking question for the human adjudication, not something for you to resolve — just verify factually how much of SFCC-96's described behaviour (mega menu two-column layout, campaign image, mobile drill-down with back control, Contentful-managed content, keyboard nav, screen reader support) the shipped code in `list-menu/` and `drawer-menu/` actually implements, so the human reviewer has an accurate factual picture of the overlap.

## Five angles — cover all of them (dispatch your own sub-agents per angle as you normally would)

1. **Correctness & regression.** Focus especially on: the `useMegaMenuMotion` phase state machine and `list-menu-popover.tsx`'s CSS-driven height/opacity choreography; `useHeaderNav.ts` (there's a self-documented, still-open "locale bug" mentioned repeatedly in this branch's own build notes — find and characterize it precisely, don't just take the label at face value); the mobile drill-down state (`useDrawerMenuState`, L1/L2 focus management). Also independently verify two things I already traced through the source myself (confirm or correct my read, don't just take my word):
   - `overrides/app/components/drawer-menu/index.tsx`: `DrawerMenuView` (line ~132) destructures `onLogoClick: _onLogoClick = noop` and never calls it — dead end. The container `DrawerMenu` (line ~254) *does* correctly thread its own `onLogoClick` prop through to `<DrawerMenuView onLogoClick={onLogoClick} .../>`, so the callback arrives faithfully and is then silently dropped by the presentational component. `DrawerMenuProps`'s own doc comment (line ~236) claims "ignored except isOpen/onClose/onLogoClick" — check whether that comment is simply inaccurate (onLogoClick behaves as ignored too, since nothing renders a logo inside the drawer at all — LeftBar owns the visible logo even in the mobile-open state) or whether there's a real missing wire-up.
   - `overrides/app/components/header/rightBar/index.tsx`: `storeLocatorEnabled`/`onStoreLocatorClick` props are declared, destructured, and never used anywhere in the render. Check whether there's any code path that does use them that lint might have missed, and note this for the styling/conventions angle too (see below).

2. **Conventions, structure, and tier ownership.** Cross-check against `.claude/rules/conventions.md`, `components.md`, `typescript.md`, `css.md`, `overrideStyling.md`. Specifically check: `overrides/app/constants/index.ts` gained one new line, a generic `TODO: Review this file and remove any constants that are not used.` comment appended to the license header block — this repo's own build notes for this branch flagged this exact comment as unexplained/unattributed ("nobody in this conversation added it") and never resolved it. Judge it on its own merits against this repo's comment-hygiene conventions (AGENTS.md: comments only when the WHY is non-obvious; this one explains nothing). Also verify the co-located `<name>.css.ts` recipes this PR adds (header.css.ts, leftBar.css.ts, rightBar.css.ts, list-menu.css.ts, megaMenuContent.css.ts, drawer-menu.css.ts) are registered correctly in `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` and follow the co-location governance pattern in overrideStyling.md (namespacing, no bare Chakra token keys — recipeGuards.test.ts already covers the mechanical part and passes, but check for anything that guard can't see, like a bare key used as a JSX/`sx` prop rather than inside a registered recipe).

3. **Contract fidelity.** `header/`, `list-menu/`, `drawer-menu/` are all Tier 2 "Global Shell" components per `.claude/rules/protectedFiles.md`. Check `overrideStyling.md`'s "SFCC bridge pattern" section: if `list-menu`/`drawer-menu` are consumed internally by base SFCC components (grep `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/` for imports of these paths), their default export needs to stay a faithful, prop-compatible port. `DrawerMenuProps` and presumably an equivalent for `ListMenu` claim call-site compatibility with base `_app.jsx` — verify that claim against what `_app.jsx` (or wherever the base template actually renders these) really passes in, and flag any prop the base caller sends that this override silently ignores in a way that could break something real (as opposed to genuinely-dead props like the logo click case above, which appears harmless because nothing needs it).

4. **Failure modes & security.** `useHeaderNav.ts` fetches Contentful data — check what renders if that fetch fails or Contentful is down (AGENTS.md's Graceful Degradation: each external system must fail independently, no blank/broken header). Check every place CMS-sourced content (nav labels, promo image alt text, editorial link text/hrefs) gets rendered for any raw HTML injection path (`dangerouslySetInnerHTML` must always be wrapped in a sanitizer per conventions.md — confirm none of the new nav/mega-menu/drawer code introduces an unsanitized one). Check `.storybook/preview.tsx`'s new `window.__CONFIG__` shim is genuinely gated to Storybook only (`typeof window !== 'undefined'` inside a file that only ever runs in Storybook) and can't leak into the real SSR/client bundle.

5. **Token and styling strategy.** Confirm the `footer.css.ts:20` audit-tokens violation from the gate numbers above is real and not a script false-positive. Spot-check the newer recipes (`zimmSearchInput.css.ts`, `rightBar.css.ts`, `leftBar.css.ts`, `megaMenuContent.css.ts`, `drawer-menu.css.ts`) for hardcoded hex/px/rem/em values that the audit script's regex might not catch (e.g. inside a template literal or computed string) or bare Chakra token keys used as a JSX/`sx` prop rather than in a registered recipe (recipeGuards.test.ts's mechanical guard only walks the registered recipe map, not JSX — see css.md's own note on this gap). Also check whether `gridSystem.ts`'s new `--zimm-grid-max-width`/`--zimm-grid-margin-*` tokens are consumed consistently everywhere they should be now that both header and footer share them, or whether one of the two drifted.

## Output
Report findings per angle, each with file:line, a concrete failure scenario (not just "this looks off"), and your confidence. I will independently verify everything through zm-scorer before anything goes to the human reviewer, so surface everything you find rather than self-filtering — including anything that contradicts what I've told you above.

4	export type DrawerMenuStateContextValue = {
5	  /** The L1 item currently drilled into, or `null` at L1. Only meaningful while `isDrilledIn`
6	   * is true — DrawerMenu reads this to know which item's columns to render as its L2 panel. */
7	  activeItem: HeaderNavItemEntry | null;
8	  /** Whether the drawer is showing the L2 (drilled-in) panel rather than the L1 root list. */
9	  isDrilledIn: boolean;
10	  /** Called by DrawerMenu when the shopper taps an L1 row that has columns (drills to L2). */
11	  drillInto: (item: HeaderNavItemEntry) => void;
12	  /** Called by DrawerMenu whenever its own `isOpen` prop (owned by base `_app`'s
13	   * `useDisclosure`, not by this hook — see useHeaderMenuExpandedState's own comment)
14	   * transitions to false. Keeps the header shell's chrome state in sync no matter how the
15	   * physical drawer actually closed (LeftBar/RightBar's own close controls, Escape, or an
16	   * overlay click all eventually flow through here). */
17	  notifyClosed: () => void;
18	  /** DrawerMenu registers its real `onClose` prop (the one it receives directly from base
19	   * `_app`) here on mount, so the header shell's LeftBar 'X' / RightBar close-icon — which
20	   * have no `onClose` prop of their own — can trigger the actual Chakra `<Drawer>` close.
21	   * Pass `null` to unregister on unmount. */
22	  registerCloseHandler: (fn: (() => void) | null) => void;
23	};
24	
25	const noop = () => undefined;

27	/**
28	 * Static default so DrawerMenu (and its presentational view) can still render standalone in
29	 * Storybook/Vitest without a header-mounted Provider — same graceful-degradation shape as
30	 * useUiCopy (see .claude/rules/components.md's Context-backed-hook exception). A story/test
31	 * that needs to exercise real drill-in/close-registration behaviour should wrap with
32	 * `DrawerMenuStateContext.Provider` instead of relying on this default.
33	 */
34	export const DEFAULT_DRAWER_MENU_STATE: DrawerMenuStateContextValue = {
35	  activeItem: null,
36	  isDrilledIn: false,
37	  drillInto: noop,
38	  notifyClosed: noop,
39	  registerCloseHandler: noop,
40	};

44	 * `useHeaderMenuExpandedState`) and `DrawerMenu`, which base `_app.jsx` renders as one of
45	 * Header's `children` (redirected to our override through the `ccExtensibility` resolver) —
46	 * not a component Header instantiates directly. Context is the tool for this rather than a
47	 * prop, since Header cannot see through whatever wrapper elements (`HideOnDesktop`, etc.)
48	 * base `_app.jsx` nests `<DrawerMenu>` inside.
49	 */
50	export const DrawerMenuStateContext = createContext<DrawerMenuStateContextValue | undefined>(undefined);

53	 * Consumed by `DrawerMenu` to read/report L1↔L2 drill state that's actually owned by the

56	 *
57	 * @returns the current drawer menu state/actions — see DrawerMenuStateContextValue.
58	 */
59	export const useDrawerMenuState = (): DrawerMenuStateContextValue =>
60	  useContext(DrawerMenuStateContext) ?? DEFAULT_DRAWER_MENU_STATE;

# PR #65 Review — Phase 2 Findings

Reviewed by direct inspection of both worktrees (no re-run of the gates you already measured), `git log`/`git show` archaeology on the PR's own commit history, `gh api` calls against the live PR/org, and a live run of `node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs` (advisory-only, not a re-run of tsc/lint/vitest) plus three targeted `npx eslint` invocations to verify specific line numbers you asked me to confirm.

---

## Angle 1 — Correctness & Regression

**🔴 MUST-FIX — CONFIRMED — ONE-OFF (but see the barrel finding below for the same root-pattern class). Store Locator entry point silently deleted, live-config-enabled today.**
- `overrides/app/components/header/rightBar/index.tsx` — `storeLocatorEnabled`/`onStoreLocatorClick` (type declared lines 65/72, destructured lines 113/119) are never referenced anywhere else in the file. Confirmed via full-file read and via `npx eslint` on the file directly (`113:3 'storeLocatorEnabled' is defined but never used`, `119:3 'onStoreLocatorClick' is assigned a value but never used`).
- This is a real regression, not scaffolding for unbuilt work: on `develop` (base worktree), `overrides/app/components/header/index.tsx:405-416` rendered a working, config-gated `<IconButton aria-label="Store Locator" ... onClick={onStoreLocatorClick}/>`, mirroring base SFCC's own `header/index.jsx:346-355`. Base (unmodified — no override exists) `_app/index.jsx:393-412` mounts a real `<StoreLocatorModal isOpen={isStoreLocatorOpen} onClose={onCloseStoreLocator}/>` and wires `<Header onStoreLocatorClick={onOpenStoreLocator}/>`. **`config/default.js:36` sets `storeLocatorEnabled: true` today** — this isn't a dormant future flag, the modal is unconditionally mounted in the live app right now. After this PR, `getConfig().app?.storeLocatorEnabled` is still computed in `header/index.tsx:149` and threaded all the way to `RightBar`, but there is no click target anywhere (`rightBar/index.tsx:426`'s own comment — "Store locator omitted from mobile — Figma node 40000307:11868 shows only search + bag" — confirms mobile is intentional per new Figma, but nothing exists at desktop/tablet either, and nothing exists anywhere else in `overrides/` — grepped for `StoreLocator`/`store-locator` across the whole tree). `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md` lists "Store Locator" as **Squad B, Sprint 5 (24 Aug–4 Sep)** — the sprint ending this week — so this collision is live risk, not hypothetical.
- Neither `rightBar/index.test.tsx:97` nor `rightBar/index.stories.tsx:85` exercise the `true` branch (`storeLocatorEnabled: false` in both) — no test would currently catch this being broken further.
- Checked CodeRabbit's full comment history on this PR for "storeLocator" — zero hits. This has not been raised or dispositioned anywhere in the existing review thread.

**🟡 SHOULD-FIX — CONFIRMED — ONE-OFF. `onLogoClick` dead-end + inaccurate doc comment (your read, corrected on one detail).**
- `overrides/app/components/drawer-menu/index.tsx:135` — `onLogoClick: _onLogoClick = noop` in `DrawerMenuView`, never called. Confirmed the container half of your read: `DrawerMenu` (line 254-282) *does* correctly thread its own `onLogoClick` down to `<DrawerMenuView onLogoClick={onLogoClick}.../>` (line 274) — the callback arrives faithfully and dead-ends only at the presentational layer.
- Your alternate hypothesis ("LeftBar owns the visible logo even in the mobile-open state") is **not** what's happening — I read `leftBar/index.tsx` in full; it renders only the hamburger/X/back icon-button plus `<chakra.nav>{children}</chakra.nav>`, no logo anywhere. The real mechanism: `header/index.tsx:256` conditionally hides Header's *entire* logo row — `{mobileMenuExpanded === 'closed' && (<chakra.div __css={styles.logoBar}>...<ZimmLogo/>...)}` — whenever the drawer is open, per Figma ("mobile 'Navigation' component drops to a 72px Exit/search/bag row with no wordmark," also documented in `drawer-menu.css.ts:36`). So there is **no logo rendered anywhere** while the drawer is open, by design — `onLogoClick` isn't redundant with something else, it's unreachable because its target element doesn't exist in that state.
- Consequence: `DrawerMenuProps`'s own doc comment (`drawer-menu/index.tsx:236-239`, "ignored except `isOpen`/`onClose`/`onLogoClick`") is factually wrong — `onLogoClick` is effectively ignored too. Low-severity (nothing is broken; a shopper never sees a broken logo click), but worth a one-line comment fix plus considering whether the prop should just be dropped from `DrawerMenuProps`/`DrawerMenuView` entirely.

**🔴 MUST-FIX — CONFIRMED — UNIFORM. Second occurrence of the "base-path import of an already-overridden component" class this repo already tracks one open instance of.**
- `overrides/app/components/list-menu/index.ts`:
  ```ts
  export { ListMenuPopover } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/list-menu/list-menu-popover';
  ```
  This barrel exports `ListMenu` from the local override (`./list-menu`, correct) and `ListMenuContent` from the base path (correct — not overridden), but `ListMenuPopover` **is** overridden by this PR (`overrides/app/components/list-menu/list-menu-popover.tsx`, 282 new lines carrying the entire open/switch/close motion choreography) and the barrel still points at the vanilla base component under that name.
  - Not currently live-broken: I checked every test/story file in `list-menu/` and confirmed all of them import `ListMenuPopover` from the correct relative path (`./list-menu-popover`) directly, bypassing this barrel. Base `_app/index.jsx` only imports `{ListMenu, ListMenuContent}` from this barrel, not `ListMenuPopover`.
  - But it's a live landmine: this is exactly the failure mode `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`'s "Importing an already-overridden component from a new component" section warns about, and it already documents one open instance (`product-tile`'s `DisplayPrice`) as "known, not yet fixed." This PR introduces a second one. Any future consumer that imports `ListMenuPopover` via `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/list-menu` (which the `ccExtensibility` resolver redirects straight to this exact barrel in the real app build) — or via `app/components/list-menu` internally — silently gets the unstyled, non-choreographed base component with no build-time signal. I flag this UNIFORM specifically because it's the *second* instance of a class this codebase has already named — worth a dedicated audit of every override barrel's re-exports, not a one-line fix.
  - Checked CodeRabbit's comment history for "ListMenuPopover"/list-menu barrel discussion — the hits that exist are about an unrelated topic (Contentful `item.id`/`href`-vs-`columns` shape ambiguity, deferred to SFCC-96). This specific barrel mis-export has not been raised.

**Locale bug — CONFIRMED, and your framing needs correcting: it's fixed, not "still open."**
The plan doc (`.docs/temp/SFCC-52-global-header-plan.md`) mentions the `useHeaderNav.ts` locale bug as "still unfixed" **five separate times**, most recently in its own top/current entry (line 3), which explicitly claims to be "the current head of the branch." I traced this via `git log`: commit `cce27da` ("fix(hooks): scope useHeaderNav's Contentful fetch to the active locale") **is** in this PR's commit range (15 commits before the tip) and genuinely fixes it — `useHeaderNav.ts:56,67` (current HEAD) includes `locale` in both the React Query key and the Contentful `getEntries()` call, using the same `siteLocale?.id ?? CONTENTFUL_FALLBACK_LOCALE` pattern already established, unmodified by this PR, in `pages/experience/index.tsx:95`. The doc is simply stale: its last touch (`7de47c5`) landed one commit *before* the fix, and 15 more commits (including unrelated SFCC-96 accessibility work merged from PR #72 and an image content-type migration from PR #73) landed after with no further doc update. **Recommend not treating this doc's "What's left" list as accurate without cross-checking each item against the current diff** — I only re-verified the locale-bug item; I did not re-verify "footer's fade underline," "provisional duration/easing values," "no mobile motion spec yet," or "L2 four-axis review for Clothing/Accessories/New" (that last one is self-disclosed as still-incomplete for 3 of 4 categories and I have no reason to doubt it, I just didn't independently re-check it).

**`useMegaMenuMotion`/`list-menu-popover.tsx` choreography — read closely, internally consistent.** The phase reducer's guards against the two documented stuck-transition risks (HOVER/CLOSE during `expanding`) are correct — `expanding`'s content opacity target never changes, so routing through `contentOut` would never fire a `transitionend`, and both reducer branches correctly special-case it. `useTransitionSafeValue`'s two-`requestAnimationFrame` deferral is sound.
- 🔵 **NOTE — PLAUSIBLE, not verified in a browser.** The file's own top comment documents that a *switch* between two L1 items snaps `grid-template-rows` straight to `1fr` with `transition: 'none'` (by design — "a switch between items must never move the height"). If the two panels have genuinely different natural content heights (build notes confirm Collections' two-column layout vs. Clothing's single-column had a 7-vs-6-link discrepancy in one Figma revision), this would produce a visible, unanimated height jump on switch — deliberate per the comment, but worth a manual check since it could read as a rendering glitch.
